final_answer:
The decimal number 0.1 can be converted to binary by repeatedly multiplying the fractional part by 2 and recording the integer parts of the results. This process yields the binary fraction 0.0001100110011..., which is a repeating, non-terminating sequence. 

The reason 0.1 cannot be represented exactly in binary is that the denominator of the fraction (10 in decimal) is not a power of 2. In binary, only fractions with denominators that are powers of 2 (e.g., 1/2, 1/4, 1/8) can be expressed as finite binary fractions. Since 10 is not a power of 2, 0.1 in decimal results in an infinite, repeating binary expansion. This is analogous to how 1/3 cannot be represented exactly in decimal, as it results in 0.333...
